22173:

Hence potassium is responsible for maintaining turgor in cells → (A)

22177:

22178:

22179:

22181:

22182:

22183:

22184:

22185:
Semiconservative replication predicts each daughter duplex keeps one parental strand plus one newly synthesised strand

The experiment used the bacterium E. coli, which is option B

22186:
Monocarpic plants flower and fruit only once in their lifetime and then die, while polycarpic plants flower repeatedly

22187:

Hence offsets arise by mitotic divisions, which is option B

22188:

22189:
Pollen grains survive as fossils because their outer exine wall resists decay, acids and high temperature
This resistance comes from sporopollenin, one of the most chemically inert biological polymers known
The inner cellulosic intine and the pollenkitt coating degrade readily and cannot preserve grains
Hence preservation is due to sporopollenin, which is option D
→ (D)
22190:
In population ecology natality means the birth rate, the number of births per unit population per unit time
Mortality is the death rate, while immigration and emigration count individuals entering or leaving the habitat
Natality adds individuals and raises population density, opposing the effect of mortality
→ (B)
22191:
The Montreal Protocol on substances depleting the ozone layer was signed on 16 September 1987
To commemorate that agreement the United Nations observes World Ozone Day every year on the same date
The day raises awareness about protecting the stratospheric ozone shield from depletion
Hence World Ozone Day is 16 September, which is option A
→ (A)
22192:
Primary pollutants enter the atmosphere directly from sources, while secondary pollutants form later by reactions among them
\text{SO}_{2}, \text{CO}_{2} and CO are emitted directly by combustion and related sources
Tropospheric ozone is generated when nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons react in sunlight, making it a secondary pollutant
Hence the secondary pollutant is tropospheric ozone, which is option D
→ (D)
22193:
Habitat is the physical address where an organism lives, while niche is its functional profession in the community
Niche covers feeding relationships, energy-flow position and the role played where the organism lives
Temperature range or physical space alone describe only part of the habitat, not the functional role
→ (D)
22194:
Ecological pyramids of biomass arrange the dry weight of each trophic level from producers upward
The data give 10 g for primary producers, 60 g for primary consumers and 120 g for secondary consumers
Values rising from producers to top consumers form an inverted pyramid of biomass
Hence the pyramid here is inverted, which is option C
→ (C)
22195:
Chlorofluorocarbons release active chlorine in the stratosphere under ultraviolet radiation
Each chlorine atom catalyses the breakdown of ozone into molecular oxygen in a repeating chain reaction
A single chlorine radical can destroy thousands of ozone molecules before being removed
→ (B)
22196:
Sugars are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones carrying several hydroxyl groups along the carbon chain
The aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group decides whether a sugar is an aldose or a ketose
Carbonyl plus hydroxyl groups together give sugars their reducing and condensation behaviour
Hence the characterising groups are carbonyl and hydroxyl, which is option D
→ (D)
22197:
Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus, while eukaryotes enclose their DNA within one
Nostoc and Oscillatoria are cyanobacteria and Mycobacterium is a bacterium, all prokaryotic
Saccharomyces is a yeast, a unicellular fungus with a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles
→ (C)
22198:
The Golgi complex receives proteins and lipids from the endoplasmic reticulum for modification and sorting
It packages the processed cargo into vesicles for secretion or delivery to their destinations
Activation of amino acids is carried out by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase in the cytosol during translation
Hence the function not occurring in the Golgi is amino acid activation, which is option B
→ (B)
22199:
The light reactions split water, releasing oxygen, and pass electrons through the photosystems
This electron flow drives photophosphorylation to form ATP and reduces \text{NADP}^{+} to NADPH
NADH belongs to respiration and fermentation pathways rather than the photosynthetic light reactions
Hence the product not formed in the light reactions is NADH, which is option B
→ (B)
22200:
Nucleolus is a non-membranous nuclear body built for rRNA transcription and ribosome assembly
During active growth it enlarges as rRNA synthesis rises, and it disperses when the cell enters division
Spindle formation is driven by the centrosome, so larger nucleoli do not mark dividing cells
The true role is therefore the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis, which is option D
→ (D)
22201:
Stomatal aperture follows guard-cell turgor driven by light-activated solute uptake and water entry
Low CO_{2} concentration opens stomata while high CO_{2} concentration closes them, and temperature tunes enzymes and transpiration
O_{2} concentration plays no direct role in this mechanism
Stomatal movement is therefore not affected by O_{2} concentration, which is option A
→ (A)
22202:
Prophase I runs through leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis in order.
Once crossing over ends, the synapsed homologues start moving apart in diplotene.
Chiasmata become visible as this desynapsis begins.
Diakinesis only completes terminalisation, so separation starts in diplotene.
→ (B)
22203:
Grass leaves carry stomata with guard cells pinched in the middle.
This constricted shape looks like a dumb-bell under the microscope.
Kidney-shaped guard cells belong to dicot leaves instead.
Grasses therefore show dumb-bell shaped stomata.
→ (C)
22204:
Secondary vascular tissues in dicot stems come from a lateral meristem.
Vascular cambium deposits secondary xylem toward the inside and secondary phloem toward the outside.
Phellogen makes periderm while apical meristems only extend length.
Secondary xylem and phloem are therefore produced by vascular cambium.
→ (B)
22205:
Saline waterlogged soils turn anaerobic and suffocate ordinary roots.
Mangrove halophytes push negatively geotropic roots upward out of the mud.
These pneumatophores exchange gases through surface pores.
Pneumatophores therefore occur in halophytes.
→ (C)
22206:
Casparian strips are suberised waterproof bands on radial walls that block apoplastic flow
They occur in the endodermis of the root, forcing water and solutes across membranes for selective uptake
Cortex, pericycle and epidermis carry no such regulatory bands
Casparian strips therefore occur in the endodermis, which is option D
→ (D)
22207:
Durable secondary thickening needs a persistent vascular cambium producing secondary xylem and phloem
Conifers and deciduous angiosperms maintain active cambia and form wood
Grasses are monocots without a true vascular cambium and show little or no secondary growth
Plants with little or no secondary growth are therefore grasses, which is option C
→ (C)
22208:
Sweet potato stores food in a swollen underground root without nodes, buds or leaves
Such a root arising from non-radicle parts of the plant is an adventitious root modification
Stems and rhizomes bear nodes and buds, while tap roots continue the primary radicle
Sweet potato is therefore a modified adventitious root, which is option B
→ (B)
22209:
Horsetails are pteridophytes, not gymnosperms, and both Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous
Cycas is typically unbranched but Cedrus shows a branched habit, so the stem pairing fails
Gymnosperms bear naked ovules carried on megasporophylls without any enclosing ovary wall
The correct statement is therefore that ovules are not enclosed by ovary wall in gymnosperms, which is option C
→ (C)
22210:
Sporozoans such as Plasmodium lack pseudopodia and locomotory organelles entirely
Mushrooms are basidiomycetes, fungal and plant walls are present, and mitochondria power all kingdoms except Monera
Claiming pseudopodia as locomotory and feeding structures in sporozoans contradicts this classification
The wrong statement is therefore the sporozoan pseudopodia claim, which is option A
→ (A)
22211:
In Agaricus karyogamy and meiosis in the basidium yield four basidiospores borne exogenously on sterigmata
Neurospora and Saccharomyces form ascospores endogenously inside asci after the same nuclear events
Alternaria reproduces by mitotic conidia without karyogamy and meiosis
Spores produced exogenously after karyogamy and meiosis therefore occur in Agaricus, which is option A
→ (A)
22212:
Herbarium keeps dried pressed plant sheets, so a matches iii.
A key booklet of alternate characters aids identification, so b matches iv.
Museum holds preserved plants and animals, so c matches i.
Catalogue enumerates area species with descriptions, so d matches ii.
→ (C)
22213:
Wind-pollinated gymnosperms lighten their grains with air sacs.
Pinus pollen carries two lateral wings for long-distance dispersal.
Mango, Cycas and mustard produce no such winged grains.
Winged pollen grains are therefore present in Pinus.
→ (D)
22214:
Gemma cups occur in Marchantia, brown algae release biflagellate zoospores, and Chlorella is unicellular
Polysiphonia is a red alga whose male gametes are non-motile spermatia without any flagellum
Pairing it with uniflagellate gametes contradicts red algal reproduction
The wrongly matched pair is therefore uniflagellate gametes and Polysiphonia, which is option C
→ (C)
22215:
Asthma is an inflammatory disorder in which the bronchioles swell and narrow, obstructing airflow through the lower airways
Emphysema permanently destroys alveolar walls, which reduces the respiratory surface available for gas exchange
The asthma to emphysema sequence is therefore inflammation of bronchioles followed by decreased respiratory surface
→ (C)
22216:
The tricuspid valve guards the right atrioventricular opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle
The bicuspid valve guards the left atrioventricular opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle
Semilunar valves guard the outlets of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and aorta, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii
→ (A)
22217:
Tidal volume is the quiet-breath volume of about 500 mL, while inspiratory reserve volume is the extra 2500 to 3000 mL that can still be inhaled
Expiratory reserve volume is the extra 1000 to 1100 mL that can still be exhaled after a quiet expiration
Residual volume is the 1100 to 1200 mL that always remains in the lungs, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
→ (B)
22218:
The transparent lens is suspended behind the iris by the suspensory ligaments called the zonules of Zinn
These zonular fibres anchor the lens capsule to the ciliary body, whose muscle varies their tension during accommodation
The iris and its muscles adjust the pupil, but they do not hold the lens in position
→ (C)
22219:
Epinephrine is synthesised from the amino acid tyrosine, so it is the amino-acid-derived hormone in this set
Estradiol and estriol are steroid hormones built from cholesterol, and ecdysone is also a steroidal hormone
Hence epinephrine is the amino-acid-derived hormone, which is option C
→ (C)
22220:
Loss of estrogen after menopause removes protection of bone density, while excess parathyroid hormone mobilises calcium out of bone
Together estrogen and parathyroid hormone changes drive the bone loss seen in osteoporosis
Hence the pair involved is estrogen with parathyroid hormone, which is option A
→ (A)
22221:
The hypothalamus produces releasing hormones and regulates temperature, hunger and thirst, so its pairing is stated correctly
The limbic system governs emotion and motivation, whereas interconnecting fibre tracts that control movement describe commissures and association fibres rather than the limbic system
Hence the limbic pairing is the incorrect one, which is option B
→ (B)
22222:
The amnion is the thin extra-embryonic membrane that encloses the fluid-filled cavity around the embryo
It forms from inner ectoderm lined on the outside by mesoderm
Hence the amnion derives from ectoderm and mesoderm, which is option C
→ (C)
22223:
Pregnancy is maintained by placental human chorionic gonadotropin, human placental lactogen, progestogens and estrogens
Relaxin is chiefly ovarian and oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary, while glucocorticoids are adrenal products
Hence the placental maintenance set is hCG, hPL, progestogens and estrogens, which is option A
→ (A)
22224:
Spermiogenesis is the differentiation of spermatids into spermatozoa without further division
Spermiation is the later step in which the mature spermatozoa are released from the Sertoli cells into the tubule lumen
Hence spermiogenesis forms spermatozoa while spermiation releases them, which is option D
→ (D)
22225:
Saheli is a non-steroidal once-a-week oral contraceptive pill, neither an IUD nor a post-coital pill
It blocks estrogen receptors in the uterus so that a fertilised egg cannot implant
Hence the correct description is the estrogen-receptor blocker, which is option C
→ (C)
22226:
Ciliates such as Paramecium are unique among protozoans in carrying two kinds of nuclei, a large macronucleus and a small micronucleus
Contractile vacuoles occur widely in freshwater protozoans, while pseudopodia and flagella characterise other groups
Hence the ciliate characteristic is two types of nuclei, which is option D
→ (D)
22227:
A storage crop followed by a muscular grinding gizzard is the hallmark digestive combination of birds
Reptiles, amphibians and bony fishes possess neither this crop nor this gizzard arrangement
Hence the crop-and-gizzard pair characterises Aves, which is option A
→ (A)
22228:
Both sexes of cockroach carry anal cerci and wing pairs with tegmina, so neither trait separates males from females
Only the male bears a pair of slender anal styles on the ninth abdominal sternum
Hence the male is identified by anal styles, which is option B
→ (B)
22229:
Homeotherms keep a constant body temperature, a group comprising all birds and all mammals
Camelus, Macropus and Psittacula are a camel, a kangaroo and a parrot, so each of them is a homeotherm
Chelone is a marine turtle, a reptile whose body temperature varies, so it is not a homeotherm
→ (B)
22230:
Moth passes through larva and pupa, tunicates change from tadpole larva to sessile adult, and starfish pass through bipinnaria larva
Earthworms hatch from cocoons as miniature adults with direct development and no larval stage
With no ecological or morphological transformation, no metamorphosis occurs here
The animal that does not undergo metamorphosis is therefore the earthworm, which is option C
→ (C)
22231:
Diatoms are unicellular photosynthetic algae forming the bulk of marine phytoplankton.
Their vast blooms fix more carbon than cyanobacteria, dinoflagellates or euglenoids in open seas.
This dominant primary production sustains most marine food chains.
Hence diatoms are regarded as the chief producers in the oceans.
→ (B)
22232:
Antibiotics such as penicillin arise when one microbe secretes a compound that inhibits a competitor
The producer gains while the susceptible microbe is harmed and the producer itself is unaffected
This zero-gain for one partner plus harm to the other defines amensalism
The interaction harnessed for antibiotic production is therefore amensalism, which is option D
→ (D)
22233:
Ex-situ conservation maintains biodiversity outside natural habitats in managed facilities
Botanical gardens, seed banks and safari parks all hold species in artificial care away from the wild
Sacred groves are community-protected natural forest patches conserved in place
The item excluded from ex-situ conservation is therefore sacred groves, which is option B
→ (B)
22234:
Eutrophication is nutrient enrichment of water bodies driving algal blooms
Sanitary landfills are engineered sites for waste disposal, while UV-B radiation causes snow blindness
Jhum cultivation is shifting slash-and-burn farming that clears forest and links to deforestation
The correct pairing is therefore a-iii, b-iv, c-i and d-ii, which is option A
→ (A)
22235:
An expanding age pyramid has its widest base in the youngest cohort
When pre-reproductive individuals exceed reproductive individuals, many new births keep entering each year
Equal classes give a stable pyramid and fewer young give a declining one
A growing population therefore has pre-reproductive individuals more than reproductive individuals, which is option C
→ (C)
22236:
Smack is chemically heroin, a diacetyl derivative of morphine
Morphine is obtained from the dried latex of unripe capsules of the poppy Papaver somniferum
Roots, flowers and leaves are not the opiate-yielding part of the plant
So the drug comes from latex, which is option B
→ (B)
22237:
An operon consists of structural genes plus regulatory DNA, the promoter and the operator
The promoter binds RNA polymerase while the operator binds the repressor protein
An enhancer is a eukaryotic regulatory element and is not part of the operon organisation
Thus the non-operon element is an enhancer, which is option A
→ (A)
22238:
A woman carries two X chromosomes and passes one of them to every child she bears.
Each son gets his only X chromosome from his mother, so he can inherit the affected one.
Each daughter also gets one X from her mother, so she can inherit it too.
Hence the affected chromosome can be inherited by both sons and daughters.
→ (D)
22239:
Hugo de Vries proposed the mutation theory of evolution
He argued new species arise by sudden large discontinuous variations, termed saltation
Gradual minor mutations and mere phenotypic fluctuations were not his mechanism
Hence the mechanism is saltation, which is option B
→ (B)
22240:
The coding strand carries the same base sequence as the RNA transcript, with T standing in for U.
Transcription therefore copies the coding sequence directly, replacing every thymine with uracil.
Changing each T in AGGTATCGCAT to U gives AGGUAUCGCAU.
Hence the transcribed mRNA sequence is AGGUAUCGCAU.
→ (C)
22241:
The proliferative phase is the estrogen-driven follicular phase that rebuilds the endometrium
The secretory phase is the progesterone-driven luteal phase after ovulation
Menstruation is the breakdown and shedding of the endometrial lining
So a-ii, b-iii, c-i holds, which is option A
→ (A)
22242:
Glycosuria is the presence of glucose in urine when blood sugar crosses the renal threshold.
Gout deposits uric acid crystals in joints, while renal calculi are masses of crystallised salts in the kidney.
Glomerular nephritis is inflammation of the glomeruli that impairs filtration.
So the matching is a-iv, b-i, c-ii and d-iii.
→ (B)
22243:
Ultrafiltration of plasma occurs across the glomerulus within the Malpighian corpuscle.
The loop of Henle sustains the medullary gradient that concentrates the urine.
Urine then travels down the ureter and is held in the urinary bladder until release.
So the matching is a-iv, b-i, c-ii and d-iii.
→ (D)
22244:
Parietal cells secrete HCl plus Castle intrinsic factor
Intrinsic factor binds vitamin B_{12} and permits its absorption in the ileum
Vitamin B_{12} is essential for DNA synthesis in developing red blood cells
So erythropoiesis depends indirectly on parietal cells, which is option D
→ (D)
22245:
Fibrinogen is the plasma clotting factor that converts to fibrin threads at the injury site so a matches ii
Globulins include immunoglobulins that mediate defence and transport functions so b matches iii
Albumin maintains colloid osmotic pressure and fluid balance so c matches i
Combination a-ii, b-iii, c-i is given in option C → (C)
22246:
Occupational respiratory disorders come from dust inhaled at the workplace
Silicosis follows chronic silica dust exposure in mining, stone and construction work
Botulism is food-borne, anthrax is infectious and emphysema is generally smoking-related
Hence the occupational disease here is silicosis, which is option B
→ (B)
22247:
In resting muscle tropomyosin masks the myosin-binding sites on the actin filament
Released Ca^{2+} binds troponin-C and shifts the troponin-tropomyosin complex aside
This exposes the active sites so cross bridges can cycle, while ATP causes detachment separately
So calcium removes the masking of active sites for myosin, which is option C
→ (C)
22248:
Nissl bodies are the basophilic granules seen in the cell body and dendrites of neurons and stain strongly for RNA
They consist of stacks of rough endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes together with free ribosomes engaged in protein synthesis
They contain no DNA, smooth endoplasmic reticulum or lipid stores so the composition is free ribosomes and RER → (D)
22249:
Glycolysis runs in the cytosol and needs NAD to accept hydrogen atoms
The enzymes of the TCA cycle are located in the mitochondrial matrix
Electron transport occurs on the inner membrane cristae, not the outer membrane
So the incorrect claim is the outer-membrane statement, which is option D
→ (D)
22250:
Submetacentric chromosomes appear L-shaped and allosomes are the sex chromosomes
Lampbrush chromosomes are the extended diplotene bivalents seen in amphibian oocytes
Polytene giant chromosomes occur in dipteran salivary glands, not in amphibian oocytes
Thus the incorrect match is the polytene entry, which is option D
→ (D)
22251:
Humans have teeth fixed in sockets, two successive sets, and varied tooth shapes
Socketed implantation is thecodont, two sets is diphyodont, varied shapes is heterodont
Pleurodont, monophyodont and homodont describe non-mammalian dentitions
Hence human dentition is thecodont, diphyodont, heterodont, which is option B
→ (B)
22252:
Nascent secretory proteins enter the rough endoplasmic reticulum where the signal peptide is cleaved and chaperone assisted folding begins
Core N linked glycosylation of these proteins also starts in the rough endoplasmic reticulum before Golgi processing
Bulk membrane phospholipid synthesis is a smooth endoplasmic reticulum function so it does not occur in the rough endoplasmic reticulum → (D)
22253:
A single mRNA can be translated by several ribosomes at the same time
Each ribosome builds its own copy of the polypeptide in succession along the strand
This beads-on-string complex is called a polysome
Nucleosome and plastidome are unrelated structures, so the term is polysome, which is option C
→ (C)
22254:
The clue is a mosquito-borne pathogen causing chronic lymphatic inflammation
Wuchereria larvae spread by Culex block lymph vessels and produce lymphedema
This filarial condition is elephantiasis, unlike ringworm, ascariasis or amoebiasis
So the disease is elephantiasis, which is option C
→ (C)
22255:
Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and vitiligo are immune attacks on the body own tissues
Alzheimer disease is a neurodegenerative disorder of plaques and tangles, not autoimmunity
It is therefore the odd one out in this list
So the non-autoimmune entry is Alzheimer disease, which is option A
→ (A)
22256:
Divergent evolution means one ancestral structure adapted to different uses
Brains, hearts and forelimbs of bat, man and cheetah share mammalian ancestry
Octopus eyes evolved independently of vertebrate eyes, so they are analogous, not homologous
Hence the non-divergent set is the eye of octopus, bat and man, which is option D
→ (D)
22257:
Lactobacillus fermentation converts milk into curd
Bacterial synthesis raises the vitamin B_{12} content of curd above that of milk
Vitamins A, D and E show no such enrichment in this conversion
So curd is richer in vitamin B 12, which is option A
→ (A)
22258:
The same skeletal plan in forelimbs of whales, bats and humans reflects common ancestry
Shared inherited structure used for different functions defines homology
Analogy and convergent evolution mean different origins arriving at similar functions
So the forelimb similarity is homology, which is option C
→ (C)
22259:
ABO grouping is set by three alleles I^{A}, I^{B} and i, a multiple-allele system
I^{A} and I^{B} are co-dominant with each other and each is dominant over i
There is no incomplete dominance or polygenic control in ABO inheritance
Thus dominance, co-dominance and multiple alleles apply, which is option B
→ (B)
